65	## Decision
66	
67	### 1. Owners register `Callable`s; owners override nothing
68	
69	An owner is any object (normally a `RefCounted`) that, during `BOOTING`, passes the kernel descriptors containing `Callable`s bound to its methods. There is no `BlockOwner` base class and nothing is overridden. Each owner method the kernel calls is declared `-> CompletionToken` and its last statement is `return ctx.complete()`.
70	
71	The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies only to overrides, so it does not touch owner methods. The context classes of § 3 add methods to their base and **override none**; a Guideline forbids overriding a context method, because an override of `complete() -> CompletionToken` would fall under the rule. This also avoids `@abstract` (documented since 4.5, not needed) and lets tests register a plain stub. That GDScript rejects at parse time a typed function with a path that has no `return` is UNVERIFIED (Verification 1); whatever it shows, the token check (§ 3) is what catches a function that aborts at run time. At registration the kernel checks every `Callable` with `is_valid()` and, where available, `get_argument_count()` against the expected arity, so a wrong signature fails boot naming the registration rather than appearing later as `INCOMPLETE`.
72	
73	### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors
74	
75	The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.
76	
77	Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.
78	
79	**`BlockDescriptor`**
80	
81	| Field | Type | Meaning |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| `block_id` | `StringName` | Unique, namespaced (e.g. `&"graph.state"`) |
84	| `owner_name` | `StringName` | Registering system, for diagnostics |
85	| `schema_version` | `int` | Bumped on any serialised-shape change |
86	| `supported_versions` | `PackedInt32Array` | Versions `restore` accepts |
87	| `block_class` | `int` enum `SIM` / `PERCEPTION_OUT` | CR-12 |
88	| `persist` | `bool` | false = derived, rebuilt after load |
89	| `persist_scope` | `int` enum `WORLD` / `PROFILE` | Required when `persist` |
90	| `scope` | `int` enum `SHARED` / `PER_PLAYER` | PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId |
91	| `gameplay` | `bool` | The paused-write test (CR-16) |
92	| `interpolated` | `bool` | Kernel runs `commit_baseline` at P4 |
93	| `repl_hint` | `int` enum `HOST_ONLY` / `SHARED_SUMMARY` / `OWNER_PRIVATE` | Unused until VS-B, mandatory now |
94	| `restore_after` | `Array[StringName]` | DAG for ADR-0016 |
95	| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | `Callable` | Mandatory |
96	| `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` | `Callable` | Mandatory iff `interpolated` |
97	| `init_world`, `binding_source` | `Callable` | Optional (the binding source is this field only, never a separate registration) |
98	
99	**`CommandTypeDescriptor`** (complete; ADR-0002 owns the meaning of each field)
100	
101	| Field | Type |
102	|---|---|
103	| `type` | `StringName` |
104	| `owner_name` | `StringName` |
105	| `allowed_origins` | `int` bitmask (`ORIGIN_PLAYER = 1`, `ORIGIN_SYSTEM = 2`) |
106	| `actor_binding` | `int` enum `NONE` / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` |
107	| `actor_source` | `StringName` (block id; empty iff `NONE`) |
108	| `coalesce` | `int` enum `NONE` / `LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` |
109	| `max_age_ticks` | `int` |
110	| `allowed_when_paused` | `bool` |
111	| `writes_blocks` | `Array[StringName]` |
112	| `payload_schema` | `Dictionary` (authoring form; compiled at registration, ADR-0002 § 3) |
113	| `validate`, `apply` | `Callable` |
114	
115	**`HookDescriptor`**: `hook_id: StringName`, `owner_name: StringName`, `divisor: int` (≥ 1), `offset: int` (0 ≤ offset < divisor), `after: Array[Dictionary]` each `{&"id": StringName, &"tolerates_stale": bool}`, `callable: Callable`.
116	
117	**`DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor`** (CR-6 via the Debug Overlay's E-DO-38): the field list is ADR-0031's; registration is here.
118	
119	### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant
120	
121	Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call.
122	
123	```gdscript
124	class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
125	var completed: bool
126	var epoch: int
127	var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
128		get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
129	func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
130	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
131	func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it
132	
133	class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
134	func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
135	func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))
136	
137	class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
138	var tick: int
139	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
140	func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
141	class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
142	class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
143	class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
144	                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
145	class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
146	```
147	
148	`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.
149	
150	**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.
151	
152	**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. Anything else, including `null`, a type default or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).
153	
154	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
155	
156	```gdscript
157	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
158	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
159	var phase: Phase
160	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
161	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
162	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key is an opaque int; its layout is ADR-0004's
163	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
164	```
165	
166	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
167	
168	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
169	|---|---|---|
170	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
171	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
172	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
173	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
174	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
175	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |
176	
177	`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.
178	
179	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. ADR-0004 adds a debug-build check that catches a missed mark (hash each block before and after a tick and compare with whether it was marked). `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.
180	
181	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
182	
183	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
184	
185	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
186	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
187	
188	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3).
189	
190	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
191	
192	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.
193	
194	### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants
195	
196	A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.
197	
198	**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)
199	
200	| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
201	|---|---|---|---|
202	| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
203	| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
204	| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
205	| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
206	| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
207	| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
208	| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
209	| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |
210	
211	**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**
212	
213	| Local | Name | Raised when |
214	|---|---|---|
215	| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
216	| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
217	| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
218	| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
219	| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
220	| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
221	| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
222	| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
223	| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
224	| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block |
225	| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
226	| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
227	| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
228	| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
229	| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
230	| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
231	| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |
232	
233	A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.
234	
235	**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.
236	
237	Each owner's local code list is written with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward); its domain id is fixed now.
238	
239	### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet
240	
241	The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
242	
243	`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get(block_id: StringName) -> Object`, returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade. A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
244	
245	### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule
246	
247	At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:
248	
249	1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
250	2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
251	3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
252	4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.
253	
254	**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.
255	
256	### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table
257	
258	States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).
259	
260	- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
261	- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
262	- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
263	- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
264	- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.
265	
266	The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.
267	
268	### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
269	
270	Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
271	
272	### Architecture Diagram
273	
274	```
275	BOOTING (ModuleFacet.registrar, one-way; nulled at the freeze)
276	  owner.setup(facet) ──► registrar.register_block(BlockDescriptor{... callables})
277	                         registrar.register_command(CommandTypeDescriptor)
278	                         registrar.register_hook(HookDescriptor)
279	                         registrar.register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner, XFaults.NAMES)
280	                         registrar.register_diagnostics_channel(DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor)
281	  first request_new_game / request_restore boundary:
282	     validate · check Callables · Kahn sort · stale-edge warnings · compile schedule[C] · read_view + empty_view once
283	     → registry_valid = true → LOADING     (failure: boot_validation_failed → FAULTED, registry_valid = false)
284	
285	LOADING (new game): one INIT scope → each owner's init_world(seed, scope, ctx) in restore_after order → post_restore
286	                    → binding rebuild → one ALL batch per block → RUNNING
287	
288	Per tick (main thread; contexts and scopes reused, re-armed per call)
289	  P2: ValidateContext → owner.validate(cmd, sim_views, vctx) → token? outcome?
290	      APPLY scope + ApplyContext → owner.apply(cmd, scope, actx) → mutators: open_for · write · mark_dirty · status
291	  P3: for i in schedule[T mod C]: HOOK scope + HookContext → hook(sim_views, scope, hctx) → token? faulted?
292	  any fault: scope closes (fail-closed) → kernel FAULTED: Faulted(code) · Applied(uncommitted) · Dropped(FAULTED)
293	```
294	
295	### Key Interfaces
296	
297	```gdscript
298	class_name ModuleFacet extends RefCounted            # what a simulation module gets in setup() (ADR-0001)
299	var registrar: BlockRegistrar                         # BOOTING only; set to null at the freeze
300	var views: SimViews                                   # kept after the freeze
301	var fault_domain: int                                 # the module's static DOMAIN_ID
302	# Other owners' published mutator objects are wired by the composition root into the module's
303	# own setup() arguments (for example Assembly receives Graph, Layout, Body and Interaction).
304	
305	class_name BlockRegistrar extends RefCounted          # forwards to the kernel; BOOTING only
306	func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void
307	func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void
308	func register_hook(desc: HookDescriptor) -> void
309	func register_fault_domain(domain_id: int, owner_name: StringName, names: Array[StringName]) -> void
310	func register_diagnostics_channel(desc: DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor) -> void
311	
312	class_name CompletionToken extends RefCounted
313	var epoch: int
314	
315	class_name MutatorStatus extends RefCounted           # constants only
316	const OK: int = 0
317	const REFUSED: int = 1                                 # scope not open: violation, never escalated
318	
319	# Owner callable shapes (Callables; the last statement of each is `return ctx.complete()`):
320	#   validate(cmd: Command, views: SimViews, ctx: ValidateContext) -> CompletionToken
321	#   apply(cmd: Command, scope: WriteScope, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken
322	#   hook(views: SimViews, scope: WriteScope, ctx: HookContext) -> CompletionToken
323	#   init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
324	#   snapshot(ctx) / restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx) / post_restore(ctx) /
325	#   default_state(ctx) / read_view(ctx) / empty_view(ctx) / commit_baseline(ctx) /
326	#   snap_baseline(key: int, ctx) / binding_source(ctx)                            -> CompletionToken
327	#   result and control-outcome handlers (ADR-0002): (record, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken
328	
329	class_name GraphFaults extends RefCounted              # one per domain, own file; never instantiated
330	const DOMAIN_ID: int = 3
331	const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1        # pre-packed; mutators return -NOT_IN_SCOPE on a defect
332	const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"NOT_IN_SCOPE"]
333	```
334	
335	Each `class_name` above is its own file; the block shows them together for reading.
336	
337	### Implementation Guidelines
338	- **Must** register blocks, commands, hooks, fault domains and diagnostics channels only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register after the freeze.
339	- **Must** declare every kernel-invoked owner callable `-> CompletionToken` with `return ctx.complete()` as its **last** statement and nothing after `complete()` in that expression; **must never** declare one `-> void`, return a domain value, or use `assert()` or an engine error for control flow.
340	- **Must** report outcomes through `ctx` (`ok`/`reject`/`put`/`fault`); **must never** signal success or failure through the return value.
341	- **Must never** override a `CallContext` method in a subclass; subclasses only add methods.
342	- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(<its block>)` and mark dirty keys with `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator; **must never** rely on a property setter for dirty tracking, and **must never** write a block outside a scope.
343	- **Must** return a status from every Class A mutator (`OK`, `REFUSED`, or `-code`) and deliver data through a caller-owned `out` object; **must** stop and `return ctx.complete()` at the first non-`OK` status, with no second `ctx.fault`.
344	- **Must** make `restore` copy into the existing block object; **must never** replace the block object a facade wraps.
345	- **Must** keep block objects `RefCounted` and plain-data; **must never** make a block a `Resource` or `Node`, or hand out a live container from a view.
346	- **Must** declare fault codes pre-packed in the owner's `*_faults.gd` with its static `DOMAIN_ID`; **must never** reuse or renumber a code.
347	- **Must** declare `tolerates_stale` on every `after` edge between hooks that do not always coincide.
348	- **Must** keep every hook allocation-free in steady state; **must** call kernel callables with `Callable.call()` and a fixed argument list, **never** `callv` on the hot path.
349	- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable` and owners drop their facets; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value.
350	- **Must never** let an owner callable subscribe to notifications (CR-10).
351

## Decision

### 1. Owners register `Callable`s; owners override nothing

An owner is any object (normally a `RefCounted`) that, during `BOOTING`, passes the kernel descriptors containing `Callable`s bound to its methods. There is no `BlockOwner` base class and nothing is overridden. Each owner method the kernel calls is declared `-> CompletionToken` and its last statement is `return ctx.complete()`.

The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies only to overrides, so it does not touch owner methods. The context classes of § 3 add methods to their base and **override none**; a Guideline forbids overriding a context method, because an override of `complete() -> CompletionToken` would fall under the rule. This also avoids `@abstract` (documented since 4.5, not needed) and lets tests register a plain stub. That GDScript rejects at parse time a typed function with a path that has no `return` is UNVERIFIED (Verification 1); whatever it shows, the token check (§ 3) is what catches a function that aborts at run time. At registration the kernel checks every `Callable` with `is_valid()` and, where available, `get_argument_count()` against the expected arity, so a wrong signature fails boot naming the registration rather than appearing later as `INCOMPLETE`.

### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors

The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.

Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.

**`BlockDescriptor`**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | `StringName` | Unique, namespaced (e.g. `&"graph.state"`) |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` | Registering system, for diagnostics |
| `schema_version` | `int` | Bumped on any serialised-shape change |
| `supported_versions` | `PackedInt32Array` | Versions `restore` accepts |
| `block_class` | `int` enum `SIM` / `PERCEPTION_OUT` | CR-12 |
| `persist` | `bool` | false = derived, rebuilt after load |
| `persist_scope` | `int` enum `WORLD` / `PROFILE` | Required when `persist` |
| `scope` | `int` enum `SHARED` / `PER_PLAYER` | PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId |
| `gameplay` | `bool` | The paused-write test (CR-16) |
| `interpolated` | `bool` | Kernel runs `commit_baseline` at P4 |
| `repl_hint` | `int` enum `HOST_ONLY` / `SHARED_SUMMARY` / `OWNER_PRIVATE` | Unused until VS-B, mandatory now |
| `restore_after` | `Array[StringName]` | DAG for ADR-0016 |
| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | `Callable` | Mandatory |
| `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` | `Callable` | Mandatory iff `interpolated` |
| `init_world`, `binding_source` | `Callable` | Optional (the binding source is this field only, never a separate registration) |

**`CommandTypeDescriptor`** (complete; ADR-0002 owns the meaning of each field)

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `type` | `StringName` |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` |
| `allowed_origins` | `int` bitmask (`ORIGIN_PLAYER = 1`, `ORIGIN_SYSTEM = 2`) |
| `actor_binding` | `int` enum `NONE` / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` |
| `actor_source` | `StringName` (block id; empty iff `NONE`) |
| `coalesce` | `int` enum `NONE` / `LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` |
| `max_age_ticks` | `int` |
| `allowed_when_paused` | `bool` |
| `writes_blocks` | `Array[StringName]` |
| `payload_schema` | `Dictionary` (authoring form; compiled at registration, ADR-0002 § 3) |
| `validate`, `apply` | `Callable` |

**`HookDescriptor`**: `hook_id: StringName`, `owner_name: StringName`, `divisor: int` (≥ 1), `offset: int` (0 ≤ offset < divisor), `after: Array[Dictionary]` each `{&"id": StringName, &"tolerates_stale": bool}`, `callable: Callable`.

**`DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor`** (CR-6 via the Debug Overlay's E-DO-38): the field list is ADR-0031's; registration is here.

### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant

Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call.

```gdscript
class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
var completed: bool
var epoch: int
var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
	get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it

class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))

class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
var tick: int
func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
```

`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.

**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.

**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. Anything else, including `null`, a type default or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).

### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty

```gdscript
class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
var phase: Phase
var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key is an opaque int; its layout is ADR-0004's
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
```

The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.

| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
|---|---|---|
| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.

`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. ADR-0004 adds a debug-build check that catches a missed mark (hash each block before and after a tick and compare with whether it was marked). `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.

### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback

**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).

- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.

**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3).

**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.

**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.

### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants

A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)

| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |

**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**

| Local | Name | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block |
| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |

A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.

**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.

Each owner's local code list is written with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward); its domain id is fixed now.

### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet

The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).

`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get(block_id: StringName) -> Object`, returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade. A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.

### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule

At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:

1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.

**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.

### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table

States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).

- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.

The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.

### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)

Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).

### Architecture Diagram

```
BOOTING (ModuleFacet.registrar, one-way; nulled at the freeze)
  owner.setup(facet) ──► registrar.register_block(BlockDescriptor{... callables})
                         registrar.register_command(CommandTypeDescriptor)
                         registrar.register_hook(HookDescriptor)
                         registrar.register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner, XFaults.NAMES)
                         registrar.register_diagnostics_channel(DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor)
  first request_new_game / request_restore boundary:
     validate · check Callables · Kahn sort · stale-edge warnings · compile schedule[C] · read_view + empty_view once
     → registry_valid = true → LOADING     (failure: boot_validation_failed → FAULTED, registry_valid = false)

LOADING (new game): one INIT scope → each owner's init_world(seed, scope, ctx) in restore_after order → post_restore
                    → binding rebuild → one ALL batch per block → RUNNING

Per tick (main thread; contexts and scopes reused, re-armed per call)
  P2: ValidateContext → owner.validate(cmd, sim_views, vctx) → token? outcome?
      APPLY scope + ApplyContext → owner.apply(cmd, scope, actx) → mutators: open_for · write · mark_dirty · status
  P3: for i in schedule[T mod C]: HOOK scope + HookContext → hook(sim_views, scope, hctx) → token? faulted?
  any fault: scope closes (fail-closed) → kernel FAULTED: Faulted(code) · Applied(uncommitted) · Dropped(FAULTED)
```

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
class_name ModuleFacet extends RefCounted            # what a simulation module gets in setup() (ADR-0001)
var registrar: BlockRegistrar                         # BOOTING only; set to null at the freeze
var views: SimViews                                   # kept after the freeze
var fault_domain: int                                 # the module's static DOMAIN_ID
# Other owners' published mutator objects are wired by the composition root into the module's
# own setup() arguments (for example Assembly receives Graph, Layout, Body and Interaction).

class_name BlockRegistrar extends RefCounted          # forwards to the kernel; BOOTING only
func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void
func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void
func register_hook(desc: HookDescriptor) -> void
func register_fault_domain(domain_id: int, owner_name: StringName, names: Array[StringName]) -> void
func register_diagnostics_channel(desc: DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor) -> void

class_name CompletionToken extends RefCounted
var epoch: int

class_name MutatorStatus extends RefCounted           # constants only
const OK: int = 0
const REFUSED: int = 1                                 # scope not open: violation, never escalated

# Owner callable shapes (Callables; the last statement of each is `return ctx.complete()`):
#   validate(cmd: Command, views: SimViews, ctx: ValidateContext) -> CompletionToken
#   apply(cmd: Command, scope: WriteScope, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken
#   hook(views: SimViews, scope: WriteScope, ctx: HookContext) -> CompletionToken
#   init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
#   snapshot(ctx) / restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx) / post_restore(ctx) /
#   default_state(ctx) / read_view(ctx) / empty_view(ctx) / commit_baseline(ctx) /
#   snap_baseline(key: int, ctx) / binding_source(ctx)                            -> CompletionToken
#   result and control-outcome handlers (ADR-0002): (record, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken

class_name GraphFaults extends RefCounted              # one per domain, own file; never instantiated
const DOMAIN_ID: int = 3
const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1        # pre-packed; mutators return -NOT_IN_SCOPE on a defect
const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"NOT_IN_SCOPE"]
```

Each `class_name` above is its own file; the block shows them together for reading.

### Implementation Guidelines
- **Must** register blocks, commands, hooks, fault domains and diagnostics channels only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register after the freeze.
- **Must** declare every kernel-invoked owner callable `-> CompletionToken` with `return ctx.complete()` as its **last** statement and nothing after `complete()` in that expression; **must never** declare one `-> void`, return a domain value, or use `assert()` or an engine error for control flow.
- **Must** report outcomes through `ctx` (`ok`/`reject`/`put`/`fault`); **must never** signal success or failure through the return value.
- **Must never** override a `CallContext` method in a subclass; subclasses only add methods.
- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(<its block>)` and mark dirty keys with `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator; **must never** rely on a property setter for dirty tracking, and **must never** write a block outside a scope.
- **Must** return a status from every Class A mutator (`OK`, `REFUSED`, or `-code`) and deliver data through a caller-owned `out` object; **must** stop and `return ctx.complete()` at the first non-`OK` status, with no second `ctx.fault`.
- **Must** make `restore` copy into the existing block object; **must never** replace the block object a facade wraps.
- **Must** keep block objects `RefCounted` and plain-data; **must never** make a block a `Resource` or `Node`, or hand out a live container from a view.
- **Must** declare fault codes pre-packed in the owner's `*_faults.gd` with its static `DOMAIN_ID`; **must never** reuse or renumber a code.
- **Must** declare `tolerates_stale` on every `after` edge between hooks that do not always coincide.
- **Must** keep every hook allocation-free in steady state; **must** call kernel callables with `Callable.call()` and a fixed argument list, **never** `callv` on the hot path.
- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable` and owners drop their facets; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value.
- **Must never** let an owner callable subscribe to notifications (CR-10).

60	## Decision
61	
62	### 1. The tick source is `_process`, in one host node
63	
64	A single `KernelHost` node (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`) owns a `TickDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls it from its own `_process(delta)`. The host does one thing with the engine's `delta`: it converts it once, `delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0))`, and passes the integer to the driver. That conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads **that reach the simulation** (kernel H9). Presentation keeps its own `_process(delta)` for `present_time`, camera smoothing and cosmetic accumulators (Pipeline PR-9; Chart Table CT-43) and may read the committed tick `T` where the sim also computes the value (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27); none of that feeds back into the simulation. The driver is exactly the one specified in kernel CR-1a and D.5: an integer accumulator in units of microseconds × `TICK_RATE` (`TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 per tick), a boundary service before any tick, `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)`, a re-read of the kernel state after every `step()`, lag forgiveness (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0), result flush, and the paused service. This ADR does not restate those rules; the GDD is their authority. It records the *placement* and *order* decisions below.
65	
66	**The physics callback is not the clock and is not used by any simulation or presentation code in the MVP.** No script in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/` defines `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`; `physics_interpolation` stays off. The kernel does not read `physics_jitter_fix`, `physics_ticks_per_second` or `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, and nothing is coupled to them, **but they can shape the `delta` the host receives** (the engine's main-loop timer sync produces both, UNVERIFIED), so the spike logs delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 and at 0. Determinism does not depend on it, because replays inject `delta_us`. A boot check records `physics_ticks_per_second != TICK_RATE` in the diagnostics header as information, not as a failure. A later Vertical Slice physics projection (ADR-0033) runs in `_physics_process` as a read-only PROJECTOR and never steps the kernel.
67	
68	### 2. Frame order is fixed by named priority constants
69	
70	Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by three constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:
71	
72	```gdscript
73	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted
74	
75	## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
76	const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
77	const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush
78	const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; every presentation node, so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
79	```
80	
81	The three-step order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.
82	
83	Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
84	- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk**: every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, and every INPUT_SURFACE, `KernelHost` and presentation node has the default (main-thread) `process_thread_group`, because a sub-thread group leaves the main-thread ordering and breaks the main-thread rule. Exactly which rules the lint tool can enforce statically and which move to boot walks is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
85	- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
86	- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
87	- Code in `src/sim/` and `src/presentation/` does not `await get_tree().process_frame` (that signal fires outside the per-node ordering, UNVERIFIED); waiting is expressed in ticks or in `present_time`.
88	
89	### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`
90	
91	The Adapter (an INPUT_SURFACE, Player Controller GDD PC-1(a)) reads device state and calls `submit()` from its `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. It may latch raw events in `_input`/`_unhandled_input`, which the engine delivers before the frame's `_process` calls, but it submits only from `_process`. Its commands are therefore queued before the driver's boundary service and tick loop run, so an intent sampled in frame N sits in tick T's P1 batch, is applied in P2 and is integrated in P3 of the same tick: one tick of latency, never two. The Adapter never samples in `_physics_process`. Devices are identified by event type, not by `device == 0` (4.7 changed mouse and keyboard device IDs; ADR-0019).
92	
93	In a frame that runs several ticks (catch-up), the Adapter has submitted once, so only the first tick of that frame sees new commands. Continuing movement survives because intent state lives in `controller.state` and commands are edge- or change-based, not per-tick.
94	
95	### 4. `tick_alpha` is the only value presentation reads *from the driver*
96	
97	At the end of each driver frame the driver publishes `tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)` (identical to kernel D.3's `t_since_last_commit / tick_duration`; the casts are required, because `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int` and an unmarked `/` is integer division in GDScript, which would give 0 on every normal frame and fail the `integer_division` warning policy). It is a presentation-only float: it is not a state block, is never hashed or saved, and the simulation never reads it (kernel H9). Presentation reads it once per frame in its own `_process` and interpolates previous-to-current committed state with `pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)` (Pipeline Section D, interpolation formula; restore case in its Edge Cases). Because forgiveness at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0 drops whole lag ticks at the end of every frame but keeps the sub-tick remainder, `acc < TICK_UNITS` after the driver runs in `RUNNING`, so `tick_alpha` is continuous and in [0, 1). **Two rules from kernel D.3 are binding and are restated here because they are easy to lose:** (1) **while the kernel is not `RUNNING` the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0**, so a paused, loading or saving game draws the latest committed pose and never a frozen partway-back pose; (2) **on every transition into `RUNNING` the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block** (ADR-0003), so `previous == current` on resume and the first running frame, including a 0-tick frame, cannot interpolate across a discontinuity.
98	
99	Presentation also keeps a render-rate cosmetic clock, `present_time`, owned by the Pipeline root (Pipeline PR-9, ADR-0008). The rule recorded here: **cosmetic phase (flicker, gutter, fades) uses `present_time`; anything the simulation also computes (beacon aim, poses, wane) uses the kernel tick; the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase** (Lighting LO-4).
100	
101	### 5. The kernel reaches modules by injection
102	
103	There is no `Kernel` autoload and no static singleton for kernel or game state. The main scene's root script (the **composition root**, `src/game/game.gd`) constructs the kernel, the `TickDriver` and the `KernelHost`, then gives every module and subscriber **the narrowest facet it needs through `setup()`**, never the whole `Kernel`: a simulation module receives the registration and mutator-scope services ADR-0003 defines; a presentation subscriber receives `subscribe(...)`, the read views and a read-only **`PresentationClock`** (`tick_alpha`, `T`, `running`, backed by the driver); and the right to submit or to call the control plane comes only from the named handles ADR-0002 defines, which the root issues to a few objects. Handing the whole kernel to presentation would give it `submit()`, which kernel CR-10 limits to INPUT_SURFACE. Headless tests construct their own kernel, driver and facets and need no scene. In the code examples in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `Kernel.` reads as "the injected facet". There are no recorded exceptions.
104	
105	### 6. Pause, load and the tree
106	
107	The kernel's `PAUSED` state is the only pause the simulation knows (kernel CR-16). `KernelHost` is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, so the driver keeps running its boundary service whether or not anything pauses the scene tree, and no simulation code reads `SceneTree.paused`. Whether the UI layers use `SceneTree.paused` or per-layer `process_mode` is **not decided here**: the Chart Table GDD routes it to its own ADR candidate (a) and the Debug Overlay GDD (E-DO-48, AC-DO-174) assumes `SceneTree.paused` can be true; ADR-0030 decides it, and it must keep `KernelHost` and the Input Adapter `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. Window focus loss, an OS-level stall, a debugger break or a long load simply produces one large `delta`: the cap (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) and forgiveness absorb it, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`, so loads, saves and pauses never cause catch-up bursts afterwards (kernel CR-1a).
108	
109	### Architecture Diagram
110	
111	```
112	Engine main loop, one rendered frame (_process in ascending process_priority)
113	│
114	├─ -100  Input Adapter           [INPUT_SURFACE]   reads input → surface.submit(...)  (SurfaceHandle, ADR-0002)           (queued only)
115	│
116	├─  -50  KernelHost._process(delta)
117	│          delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta × 1e6))                  ← the only wall-clock read that reaches the sim
118	│          TickDriver.frame(delta_us):
119	│            1 boundary service (SAVING/LOADING/pause/resume; may clear acc, discard this frame's delta)
120	│            2 repeat ticks_run times, re-reading kernel state after each:
121	│                 Kernel.step() = P0 begin · P1 intake · P2 dispatch · P3 step hooks · P4 commit · P5 notify · P6 boundary
122	│            3 forgiveness (drop whole lag ticks, keep the sub-tick remainder)
123	│            4 flush the result buffer
124	│            5 if PAUSED: paused service
125	│          tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0, 1)   (1.0 while not RUNNING)
126	│
127	└─   0   Presentation nodes      [PRESENTATION]    handlers already marked dirty at P5;
128	           (Pipeline root, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Trail,        draw from committed views at tick_alpha;
129	            Instruments, HUD, Audio, Debug)                          Pipeline writes camera in frame_pre_draw
130	
131	_physics_process: not used by the kernel, simulation or presentation in the MVP.
132	```
133	
134	### Key Interfaces
135	
136	```gdscript
137	class_name TickDriver extends RefCounted
138	## Turns an injected wall-time delta into whole kernel ticks. No scene tree, no engine clock.
139	func _init(kernel: Kernel, params: TickParams) -> void
140	func frame(delta_us: int) -> TickFrameResult   # boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, flush; returns ticks_run, dropped, tick_alpha
141	var tick_alpha: float:                         # presentation-only; read once per frame
142		get: return _tick_alpha
143	
144	class_name KernelHost extends Node
145	func setup(driver: TickDriver) -> void         # called by the composition root; sets process_mode and process_priority
146	func _process(delta: float) -> void            # returns at once if setup() has not run (null driver); else delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0)); driver.frame(delta_us)
147	
148	class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted  # constants shown in Decision § 2
149	
150	# Every module and subscriber:
151	func setup(facet: ModuleFacet) -> void         # the narrowest facet for the module's class (ADR-0003 / ADR-0009); stored; never looked up through a global
152	
153	class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted  # read-only, backed by the TickDriver
154	var tick_alpha: float:
155		get: return _driver.tick_alpha                 # 1.0 while the kernel is not RUNNING
156	var T: int:
157		get: return _kernel_clock_t()                  # last committed tick
158	var running: bool:
159		get: return _kernel_running()
160	```
161	
162	### Implementation Guidelines
163	- **Must** drive `Kernel.step()` only from `TickDriver.frame()`, and call `TickDriver.frame()` only from `KernelHost._process`. Tests may call either directly.
164	- **Must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/`.
165	- **Must** use the `ProcessPriority` constants; **must never** write a literal `process_priority` value.
166	- **Must** submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`; **must never** call `submit()` from `_input`, `_physics_process` or a signal handler.
167	- **Must** pass each module its facet with `setup()`; **must never** add an autoload, a static variable or a group lookup that exposes the kernel, a block or a read view, and **must never** give a presentation node the whole `Kernel`.
168	- **Must** read `tick_alpha` through `PresentationClock` in presentation only, never in a simulation callable, and **must never** use the tick counter for cosmetic animation phase.
169	- **Must** keep `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` in release builds; a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise. A boot assertion also requires `application/run/low_processor_mode` to be false (in low-processor mode the engine idles between events, the simulation would stall and the next `delta` would spike), and the diagnostics header records `Engine.max_fps`, the vsync mode and `physics_ticks_per_second`.
170	- **Must** keep the `delta_us` conversion in `KernelHost` and nowhere else; the lint for forbidden clock APIs (`Time.get_ticks_msec`, `Time.get_ticks_usec`, `get_process_delta_time`, `OS.get_unix_time*`) allow-lists only `KernelHost` and the diagnostics timer. (`OS.get_ticks_*` no longer exists in Godot 4; see `deprecated-apis.md`.)
171	- **Should** test the driver with injected `delta_us` sequences (16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs patterns, 100 ms hitches, zero-length frames) and the frame order with a recording scene (KRN-LAT-01, KRN-LAT-02).
172

19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Core (frame loop, node processing order), with an Input boundary |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Every API used predates the 4.3 cutoff, but the pinned engine reference is silent on cross-node `process_priority` order and on how `Engine.time_scale` scales `_process(delta)`, and 4.7 changed input device IDs. |

(2) `Engine.time_scale` scaling of `delta` (the kernel GDD marks it UNVERIFIED). (3) The first-frame `delta` after a long block (scene load, window drag, focus loss, a debugger breakpoint) is finite and handled by the cap and forgiveness, not a crash; the boundary service discards the first frame after a load (CR-1a). (3a) Delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 versus 0, with `application/run/delta_smoothing` on and off, and the cost of the empty 60 Hz physics tick in an empty-scene baseline; the decision is to leave all three at engine defaults and record the measured effect on the 0-tick/2-tick frame pattern and on latency, not to claim they have nothing to do with the tick (MainTimerSync may adjust the idle step as well as the physics step, UNVERIFIED). (3b) `_input` and `_unhandled_input` are delivered before the frame's `_process` calls (UNVERIFIED in the reference), checked in the same scene as KRN-LAT-02. (4) `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` in the frame (owned by ADR-0008; recorded here because the camera write depends on this order). |

236	## Performance Implications
237	- **CPU**: The driver itself is an integer add, a divide and a loop; it is negligible against the kernel's budgets (P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99; frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four), which are measured on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. At 30 fps (RM-DECK) a frame normally runs two ticks; the 4-tick cap means slow motion begins below 15 fps.
238	- **Memory**: One `TickDriver`, one `KernelHost` node, a few integers. No per-frame allocation in the driver (`TickFrameResult` is reused).
239	- **Load Time**: None. The accumulator is cleared when load finishes, so load time is not repaid as ticks.
240	- **Network**: None at MVP. In VS-B a MIRROR kernel uses the same driver with no authority over commands (ADR-0002, ADR-0032).

18	## Engine Compatibility
19	
20	| Field | Value |
21	|-------|-------|
22	| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
23	| **Domain** | Core (command ingress and authority), with a Networking boundary kept dormant until VS-B |
24	| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Nothing used here is post-cutoff, but `var_to_bytes` size behaviour for payload checks, `Variant.Type` coverage and the 4.7 peer-id behaviour of `MultiplayerAPI` are not covered by the pinned reference. |
25	| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript and Core rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `modules/networking.md`, `modules/input.md` |
26	| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None in the MVP. Typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4) is allowed inside the kernel but never at the payload boundary, where payloads are untyped `Dictionary` so the whitelist can inspect them. |
27	| **Verification Required** | (1) `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` is cheap enough at the admitted command rates and is a pure function of the payload's value (it is used only as a threshold; never as hash input, because the encoder's size choices for ints and floats are not a byte-stable cross-platform contract, UNVERIFIED). (2) A `Dictionary` or `Array` payload that contains itself is stopped by the depth cap (the walk recurses to depth 9 and rejects) **before** any serialisation is attempted; serialising a cyclic container is not assumed safe. (2a) A wide payload cannot burn time before the size check: the walk aborts as soon as a running upper-bound byte estimate exceeds `MAX_PAYLOAD`. (3) The peer id a `MultiplayerAPI` RPC reports for the host is `1` on 4.7.2 (VS-B only; recorded here because `HOST_PEER_ID` = 1 is baked into the binding table). (4) GDScript has no private constructors, so "only the kernel builds a `Command`" is enforced at run time (a `_sealed` flag and a ring-slot check) and also by a CI lint that greps for `Command.new()`. (5) `Callable.is_valid()` is false for a method Callable whose target object was freed, and `Callable.call()` on a freed target errors rather than skips (UNVERIFIED; both from memory). (6) Writing into a `PackedInt64Array` fetched from a `Dictionary` value mutates the stored array only through an explicit read-modify-write (UNVERIFIED across versions); the binding table avoids the question. |

10	- **Variadic arguments**: Functions can accept arbitrary parameter counts. The
11	  rest parameter is written `...name`, comes last, and is typed `Array` or left
12	  untyped — `values: Variant...` and `...values: Array[int]` do not parse
13	  ```gdscript
14	  func log_values(prefix: String, ...values: Array) -> void:
15	      for v in values:
16	          print(prefix, ": ", v)
17	  ```

19	- **Lambdas capture local variables by value** (every Godot 4 version): a local
20	  is captured once, when the lambda is created, and a lambda cannot reassign an
21	  outer local — `var hit := false` / `func(): hit = true` leaves the caller's
22	  `hit` false. Share state through a reference type (a Dictionary, an Array or
23	  an object) and mutate its contents. A rest parameter works in a lambda too, so
24	  `func(...args)` connects to a signal with any number of arguments (observed on
25	  4.6.1; a one-argument lambda on a zero-argument signal errors "Method expected
26	  1 argument(s), but called with 0")

196	gdUnit4 6.2.x lists Godot 4.5 to 4.7.1 as compatible in its README

203	Observed on Godot 4.6.1 with gdUnit4 6.1.3, and the exits again on 4.7.2 with
204	6.2.2 — not in the docs:
205	- 101 is also the exit when every test passed but a test leaked orphan nodes;
206	  105 means a test script does not parse; 103 means gdUnit4 refused to run
207	  headless (`--ignoreHeadlessMode` missing). 104 is gdUnit4 refusing a Godot
208	  older than 4.3 — not reproducible on the pin.
209	- Over zero tests the runner prints `No test cases found` and exits 0.
210	- Without `--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0`, a script error opens the `-d`
211	  debugger and the run waits at a `debug>` prompt; with it, every run prints two

213	- A fresh clone has no `.godot/` class cache: run
